metadata.title: GENERAL PRINCIPLES AND TECHNIQUES IN MANAGEMENT

questions.question: According to the seminar, management is best described as the process of—
options: continuously searching for the optimum use of resources in pursuit of desired goals
controlling political activities within an organisation
questions.explanation: The material defines management as the continuous search for the optimum use of resources in pursuit of desired goals.

questions.question: Which definition of management is also presented in the seminar?
options: The process of utilizing available resources to accomplish a laid-down set of organisational objectives
The process of recruiting only qualified personnel
The process of eliminating all organisational risks
The process of enforcing disciplinary regulations
questions.explanation: Another definition given describes management as the process of utilizing available resources to accomplish a laid-down set of objectives of an organisation.

questions.question: In the context of the seminar, a principle is best understood as—
options: a set of rules that guides conduct, norms or procedure
questions.explanation: The seminar defines principles as a set of rules that guides conduct, norms or procedure.

questions.question: Which option most accurately defines technique as used in the seminar?
options: A way of achieving one's purpose skillfully
questions.explanation: The seminar defines technique as a way of achieving one's purpose skillfully.

questions.question: The seminar's combined description of General Principles and Techniques of Management emphasizes the use of rules or procedures to—
options: achieve one's purpose skillfully in controlling, directing or planning
eliminate the need for organisational objectives
questions.explanation: The course is described as a management process using rules or procedures to achieve one's purpose skillfully, particularly in controlling, directing or planning activities.

questions.question: According to the seminar, managers in both public and private sectors are faced with the task of—
options: harnessing resources while considering their continued availability, goals and environmental differences
questions.explanation: The source emphasizes the manager's task of harnessing resources, considering continued resource availability, organisational goals and differences in the environment.

questions.question: Why should managers identify management methods or techniques appropriate to a particular situation?
options: Because one technique is always inadequate
Because management techniques should contribute to attainment of organisational or societal goals in a particular situation and time
Because government requires every manager to use a different technique
Because techniques are determined only by employees
questions.explanation: The seminar states that managers should identify the methods or techniques that will best contribute to attaining organisational or societal goals in a particular situation and time.

questions.question: Which of the following belongs to the internal management environment?
options: Type, size and location of the organisation
questions.explanation: The internal environment includes the type, size and location of the organisation, its objectives, managers/personnel, and technology, facilities and equipment.

questions.question: Which factor is classified under the external management environment?
options: End users or beneficiaries of the organisation's products or services
questions.explanation: End users or beneficiaries, such as clients, customers or members of the public, are identified as part of the external environment.

questions.question: An organisation's equipment, facilities and technological resources would be classified under its—
questions.explanation: Technology, facilities, equipment and tools are explicitly listed among the components of the internal management environment.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a supplier/provider in the external management environment?
questions.explanation: Suppliers or providers of funds, labour, technology or infrastructure form part of the external environment. The seminar gives statutory allocation as an example.

questions.question: An increase in the price of imported items would primarily represent which external environmental factor?
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically identifies economic variables, including increases in the price of imported items and the state of the economy, as external environmental factors.

questions.question: Which combination contains only internal environmental factors identified in the seminar?
options: Economic variables, statutory allocation and clients
Organisation type/size/location, organisational objectives and personnel
questions.explanation: The internal environment comprises the organisation's type, size and location; objectives; managers and other personnel; and technology/facilities/equipment.

questions.question: A sudden change in government fiscal policy affects an organisation's investment decisions. This illustrates the influence of the—
questions.explanation: Government policies, including fiscal or tax policies, are identified as external environmental factors capable of affecting investment or business positively or negatively.

questions.question: The seminar describes the Civil Service as an institution expected to—
options: remain unaffected by changes in government policies
act with speed and sensitivity to changes in policies and events
questions.explanation: The Civil Service is described as an organic institution expected to act with speed and sensitivity to changes in policies and events.

questions.question: The Civil Service is described in the seminar as—
options: an instrument of the Government of the day
questions.explanation: The seminar describes the Civil/Public Service as a body enjoying continuity and as an instrument of the Government of the day.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the seminar's description of the Civil Service?
options: It is composed primarily of political appointees.
It is made up of servants of the State employed in a civil capacity on a non-political career basis.
It exists only during the tenure of a particular administration.
It is primarily a private commercial organisation.
questions.explanation: The seminar describes the Civil Service as being made up of servants of the State employed in a civil capacity and on a non-political career basis.

questions.question: The Civil Service is described as being intimately devoted to—
options: policy formulation and service delivery of government
questions.explanation: The material describes the Civil Service as part of the Public Service intimately devoted to policy formulation and service delivery of government.

questions.question: Which development is identified in the seminar as contributing to the restructuring of the Nigerian Civil Service?
options: The introduction of local government elections
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies the Murtala Mohammed restructuring and refers to the associated “Great Purge” in discussing the restructuring of the Civil Service.

questions.question: Which constitutional provisions are specifically identified in the seminar as providing for the establishment of State Service and protection of pension rights?
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies Sections 206 and 210 of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) in this context.

questions.question: Which body is identified as a body concerned with implementing government policies among the management tools listed?
questions.explanation: The National Council on Establishments is listed among the tools/concepts used as management techniques in the Public/Civil Service and is described as a body to implement government policies.

questions.question: The Public Service Rules primarily—
options: provide rules and regulations guiding the operation or changes in the Service
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the Public Service Rules embody rules and regulations that guide the operation or changes in the Service.

questions.question: According to the seminar, circulars and circular letters may be issued to—
options: amend, cancel or institute new rules
questions.explanation: Circulars/circular letters are described as guidelines on rules and regulations issued regularly to amend, cancel or institute new rules, and they must be obeyed by all.

questions.question: Which statement about circulars is MOST consistent with the seminar?
options: They are optional suggestions to civil servants.
They may amend, cancel or introduce rules and are to be obeyed by all.
They apply only to political office holders.
They deal exclusively with financial matters.
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically states that circulars/circular letters may amend, cancel or institute new rules and must be obeyed by all.

questions.question: A Scheme of Service is particularly useful because it shows—
options: only the salary of each public servant
different cadres, entry requirements, progression and qualifications
questions.explanation: The seminar states that Schemes of Service show different cadres, entry, progression and qualification.

questions.question: Which management tool provides guidelines for the receipts and expenditure of government funds?
questions.explanation: Financial Instructions provide guidelines for receipts and expenditure of government funds.

questions.question: The Pension Reforms Act 2014 is presented in the seminar as representing a departure from—
options: pay-as-you-go to a contributory system of payment of retirement benefits
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the Pension Reforms Act 2014 marked a departure from the former pay-as-you-go system to a contributory system of payment of retirement benefits.

questions.question: The Service Delivery Charter is associated in the seminar with—
options: improved performance, accountability, transparency and service delivery
questions.explanation: The seminar directly links the Service Delivery Charter with improved performance, accountability, transparency and service delivery.

questions.question: Which of the following is mentioned as an institution involved in seminars, workshops and training?
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically mentions the Centre for Management Development (CMD) and Administrative Staff College of Nigeria (ASCON) as examples.

questions.question: The Ayida Panel Report is identified in the seminar primarily in connection with—
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies the Ayida Panel Report on Civil Service Reforms as a major means of restructuring the present Civil Service.

questions.question: Leadership is described in the seminar as an important role because it—
options: determines the spirit of attainment of predetermined goals
applies only to political office holders
questions.explanation: The seminar states that leadership is important in any organisation and determines the spirit of attainment of predetermined goals.

questions.question: Which statement about managers and leaders is made in the seminar?
options: No manager can be a leader.
All managers are leaders, but not all leaders are managers.
Managers and leaders are completely unrelated.
questions.explanation: The material expressly states: “all managers are leaders but not all leaders are managers.”

questions.question: Which quality of leadership is associated with seeing or thinking beyond the limits of one's followers?
questions.explanation: A good leader must be a person of vision, meaning the ability to see or think beyond the limits of followers or subordinates.

questions.question: According to the seminar, a good leader should adopt which approach when handling issues?
questions.explanation: The seminar states that a good leader should be sufficiently educated and try to adopt a democratic approach in handling issues.

questions.question: Which leadership quality is most directly associated with trustworthiness in the seminar?
questions.explanation: The material specifically states that a good leader must not be a person of doubtful integrity.

questions.question: A manager accepts that circumstances are changing and actively encourages the organisation to adapt. Which leadership quality does this BEST demonstrate?
questions.explanation: The seminar states that a good leader should not merely accept change but should be a change agent.

questions.question: Which combination BEST reflects the leadership qualities specifically identified in the seminar?
questions.explanation: The seminar states that a good leader must be fair, approachable but firm.

questions.question: During an emergency, a leader remains calm and acts decisively instead of becoming confused.
options: Ability to handle emergencies without panicking
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically states that a good leader should be able to handle emergencies without panicking.

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a problem of leadership in government?
options: Complete freedom from rules and regulations
Limited manoeuvring ability of managers arising from stipulated rules and regulations
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies the limited manoeuvring ability of managers in government arising from stipulated rules and regulations as a leadership problem.

questions.question: The multiplicity of interest groups and ethnic nationalities in many Nigerian states is presented in the seminar as—
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly identifies the multiplicity of interest groups and ethnic nationalities as one of the problems of leadership in organisations.

questions.question: Which situation reflects the problem of short continuity in government policy identified in the seminar?
options: Policies remain unchanged across successive administrations.
Rapid turnover in political leadership results in frequent changes in policy direction and thinking.
Managers have complete freedom to determine government policy.
Civil servants determine all political policies.
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies short span of continuity in government policy and rapid turnover in political leadership and thinking as a leadership problem.

questions.question: MBWA, as identified in the seminar, stands for—
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies MBWA as Management by Walking Around, a management technique used in the Public Service and government business.

questions.question: The policy of commencing written promotion examinations in the Civil Service took effect, according to the seminar, from—
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the policy of commencement of written promotion examination took effect from January 2016, as conveyed by the Civil Service Commission circular letter of 9 August 2015.

questions.question: The application of the Administrative and Other Professionals Compulsory Examination to professional and other officers in the Senior Management Cadre was conveyed by—
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies CSC Circular No. 2/2017 as conveying the application of the compulsory examination to the relevant professional and other officers in the Senior Management Cadre.

questions.question: Under X Theory, employees are generally assumed to—
options: naturally enjoy work and exercise self-control
be independent and creative under the right conditions
dislike work and require close supervision
require recognition and rewards before accepting responsibility
questions.explanation: X Theory assumes, among other things, that people do not like to work and cannot work effectively without close supervision.

questions.question: Which assumption belongs to Y Theory rather than X Theory?
options: People can only work when threatened or punished.
People cannot contribute to solving organisational problems.
People require close supervision because they have no discretion.
Given the right conditions, most people can enjoy work.
questions.explanation: Y Theory takes the more positive view that, given the right conditions, most people can enjoy work and can exercise self-control, independence and creativity.

questions.question: A manager believes that employees can exercise self-control and become independent and creative when appropriate conditions exist.
questions.explanation: Those assumptions are specifically associated with Y Theory in the seminar.

questions.question: Which of the following is associated with X Theory in the seminar?
options: Recognition and rewards motivate group members.
People are naturally independent and creative.
People can only work when threatened or punished.
questions.explanation: The seminar lists the belief that people can only work when threatened or punished among the assumptions of X Theory.

questions.question: According to Y Theory, motivation is particularly necessary in a group setting where people are—
questions.explanation: The seminar states under Y Theory that motivation is necessary in a group setting where people are recognized and rewarded.

questions.question: A manager believes that employees cannot contribute meaningfully to solving organisational problems because they are not creative and must therefore be closely controlled.
options: Y Theory — motivation through recognition and reward
X Theory — reliance on supervision and punitive measures
MBWA — democratic leadership and change agency
questions.explanation: The manager's assumptions match X Theory: employees are viewed as lacking creativity, requiring close supervision and potentially responding to threats or punishment.

questions.question: The seminar describes bureaucracy, through Max Weber's view, as—
options: the least flexible form of political administration
the most efficient administrative organisation for conducting government affairs
a temporary arrangement for implementing political programmes
an organisation primarily designed for private enterprise
questions.explanation: The seminar states that Max Weber regarded bureaucracy as the most efficient administrative organisation for conducting government affairs.

questions.question: According to Weber's position as presented in the seminar, technically correct decisions are facilitated by—
options: disciplined performance governed by abstract rules and coordinated by authority hierarchy
questions.explanation: The seminar attributes technically correct decisions to disciplined performance governed by abstract rules and coordinated through an authority hierarchy, supporting rational and consistent pursuit of organisational goals.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST explains why the Civil Service is described as an institution enjoying continuity?
options: Its existence is tied to the tenure of each political administration.
It continues as an institution even as governments and political leadership change.
Its officers are elected rather than appointed.
It is independent of government policy.
questions.explanation: The seminar describes the Civil Service as a body that enjoys continuity of existence while serving as an instrument of the government of the day.

questions.question: A civil servant argues that because the Civil Service is non-political, it has no role in implementing the policies of the government of the day.
options: Correct; political neutrality means policy implementation is prohibited.
Incorrect; the Civil Service is non-political in career basis but is an instrument of the Government of the day and is devoted to policy formulation and service delivery.
Correct; only political appointees implement policy.
Incorrect only because civil servants are elected.
questions.explanation: The seminar simultaneously describes the Civil Service as non-political and career-based and as an instrument of the Government of the day, intimately involved in policy formulation and service delivery.

questions.question: Which constitutional sections are specifically associated in the seminar with the establishment of State Service and protection of pension rights?
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies Sections 206 and 210 of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) for the establishment of State Service and protection of pension rights.

questions.question: Which of the following is correctly matched with its function?
options: Financial Instructions — guidelines for government receipts and expenditure
Scheme of Service — guidelines for pension contributions only
Service Delivery Charter — classification of misconduct
Public Service Rules — determination of electoral boundaries
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically states that Financial Instructions provide guidelines for receipts and expenditure of government funds.

questions.question: A new officer wants to know the various cadres in the Service, their entry requirements, progression and qualifications.
questions.explanation: The seminar states that Schemes of Service show different cadres, entry, progression and qualifications.

questions.question: Which development represents the change from the former pay-as-you-go approach to a contributory system for retirement benefits?
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies the Pension Reforms Act 2014 (as amended) as representing this departure.

questions.question: A reform initiative is primarily concerned with improving performance, accountability, transparency and service delivery.
questions.explanation: These are the specific purposes attributed to the Service Delivery Charter in the seminar.

questions.question: The Service Delivery Charter's reform focus also seeks to ensure that the Public Service has—
options: the capacity, structures, skills and appropriate incentives to provide better services
only financial resources without regard to skills
questions.explanation: The seminar links the Charter to securing the capacity, structures, skills and right incentives needed to produce better service for the populace.

questions.question: Which institution is specifically identified as a body for implementing government policies?
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies the National Council on Establishments as a body to implement government policies.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST description of the role of circulars/circular letters in the Public Service?
options: They provide guidelines on rules and regulations and may amend, cancel or institute new rules.
They determine an officer's personal political preference.
questions.explanation: The seminar describes circulars/circular letters as guidelines on rules and regulations issued regularly to amend, cancel or institute new rules, which must be obeyed by all.

questions.question: An officer receives a properly issued circular changing an existing rule. The officer argues that compliance is optional because circulars are not the Public Service Rules themselves.
options: The officer is incorrect because the seminar states that circulars/circular letters must be obeyed by all.
The officer is correct unless the circular concerns promotion.
Compliance depends on the officer's grade level.
questions.explanation: The seminar explicitly says circulars/circular letters used to amend, cancel or institute rules must be obeyed by all.

questions.question: A circular changes the nomenclature and functional titles of certain cadres following approval in the Scheme of Service.
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically refers to the SSG Circular of 14 July 1998 concerning realignment of nomenclature and functional titles of some cadres approved in the Scheme of Service.

questions.question: SSG Circulars Nos. 1–6 of 2017 and SSG Circular 2/2003 are discussed in relation to—
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies these circulars in connection with Ministerial Responsibilities and the structuring of duties between Ministries and the Governor's Office.

questions.question: Under the arrangement described in the seminar, Ministries are generally regarded as having—
questions.explanation: The seminar describes the responsibilities of other Ministries as Mono-function (single), in contrast with the Governor's Office, described as heterogeneous or dual-functions.

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a responsibility of the Governor's Office under the heterogeneous/dual-function arrangement?
options: Every routine function of every Ministry
Preparation of every Scheme of Service
Administration of every local government office
questions.explanation: The seminar lists Prerogative of mercy among the responsibilities associated with the Governor's Office.

questions.question: Which pair consists entirely of responsibilities listed under the Governor's Office?
options: Prerogative of mercy and State Security Matters/Public Safety
Scheme of Service and financial auditing
questions.explanation: Both Prerogative of mercy and State Security Matters and Public Safety are expressly listed among the Governor's Office responsibilities.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT among the Governor's Office responsibilities specifically listed in the seminar?
options: Relations with the Presidency and National/State Assemblies
Relations with Armed Forces and Police
Preparation of all departmental annual budgets
questions.explanation: The listed responsibilities include constitutional matters, relations with the Presidency/Assemblies, prerogative of mercy, security/public safety, appointment of key public functionaries and relations with the Armed Forces and Police. Preparation of all departmental annual budgets is not listed.

questions.question: The seminar describes a manager's ability to manoeuvre in government as limited partly because of—
options: stipulated rules and regulations governing government business
questions.explanation: The limited manoeuvring ability of managers resulting from stipulated rules and regulations is expressly identified as a leadership problem.

questions.question: Which leadership problem arises from the need to align constitutional government objectives with the interests of the ruling political party and individual operators of government affairs?
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies the tension between constitutional government objectives, the interests of the ruling political party and those of individual operators of government affairs as a leadership problem.

questions.question: According to the seminar, which combination contributes to a vicious circle of corruption?
options: High-level poverty and absence of patriotic mentality
questions.explanation: The seminar directly links high-level poverty and absence of patriotic mentality with a vicious circle of corruption.

questions.question: A government repeatedly changes policy direction because political leadership changes rapidly.
options: Short span of continuity in government policy
Absence of a Scheme of Service
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly identifies short span of continuity in government policy and rapid turnover in political leadership and thinking as a leadership problem.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT presented as a problem of leadership in the organisation?
options: Multiplicity of interest groups and ethnic nationalities
High level of poverty and absence of patriotic mentality
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies limited managerial manoeuvring, not unlimited discretion, as a leadership problem.

questions.question: The seminar says a leader should be fair, approachable but firm. Which situation BEST reflects all three qualities?
options: A manager avoids every disciplinary decision to remain approachable.
A manager applies the same standard, listens to staff concerns and still enforces legitimate decisions.
A manager imposes decisions without hearing anyone.
A manager allows only close associates to approach him.
questions.explanation: The seminar explicitly identifies being fair, approachable but firm as a quality of good leadership. The scenario combines all three elements.

questions.question: A leader accepts an organisational change but takes no action to help staff adapt to it.
questions.explanation: The seminar says a good leader should not only be willing to accept change but should be a change agent.

questions.question: Which quality is most directly associated with a leader's ability to think beyond the limits of followers?
questions.explanation: The seminar defines vision in leadership as the ability to see or think beyond the limits of followers or subordinates.

questions.question: The seminar describes leadership as highly behavioural and requiring all of the following EXCEPT—
questions.explanation: The seminar associates leadership with intelligence, communication, moral building, motivation, human relationships, charisma and maturity. Isolation is not identified.

questions.question: Which statement accurately reflects the relationship between management and leadership according to the seminar?
options: Every leader must be a manager.
Every manager is a leader, but leadership can exist without managerial status.
Managers and leaders are mutually exclusive.
Only political leaders qualify as leaders.
questions.explanation: The seminar's explicit formulation is that all managers are leaders but not all leaders are managers.

questions.question: A manager is highly intelligent but repeatedly loses control during emergencies.
options: Ability to handle emergencies without panicking
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically states that a good leader should be able to handle emergencies without panicking.

questions.question: The seminar identifies MBWA as a management technique used in—
questions.explanation: Management by Walking Around (MBWA) is specifically identified as a management technique in both the Public Service and Government Business.

questions.question: Which description BEST captures MBWA as named in the seminar?
questions.explanation: MBWA is explicitly expanded as Management by Walking Around.

questions.question: The written promotion examination policy in the Civil Service took effect from—
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the written promotion examination policy took effect from January 2016, as conveyed by the Civil Service Commission circular letter of 9 August 2015.

questions.question: Which document is specifically associated with the written promotion examination policy taking effect in January 2016?
options: Civil Service Commission circular letter of 9 August 2015
questions.explanation: The seminar explicitly connects the January 2016 commencement with the Civil Service Commission circular letter of 9 August 2015.

questions.question: CSC Circular No. 2/2017 concerns the application of—
options: Financial Instructions to all junior officers
Administrative and other professionals' compulsory examination to relevant senior-management officers
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies CSC Circular No. 2/2017 in connection with applying the Administrative and Other Professionals Compulsory Examination to professional and other officers in the Senior Management Cadre.

questions.question: The seminar asks participants to consider whether recent policies such as the written promotion examination and compulsory examination are—
questions.explanation: The material explicitly tells participants to note the reasons for the above policies and consider whether they are good policies.

questions.question: Which statement about X Theory is most consistent with the seminar?
options: Employees are assumed to naturally enjoy work.
Employees are assumed to be capable of independence and creativity.
Employees are assumed to dislike work and require close supervision.
Employees are assumed to need only recognition and rewards.
questions.explanation: X Theory is presented as the punitive-measure principle and assumes that people do not like work and require close supervision.

questions.question: A supervisor believes that workers cannot effectively perform without close supervision and cannot contribute creatively to solving organisational problems.
questions.explanation: Those assumptions are explicitly listed under X Theory.

questions.question: Which assumption would be inconsistent with X Theory as presented in the seminar?
options: People do not like to work.
People cannot work effectively without close supervision.
People cannot contribute to solving organisational problems.
People are naturally independent and creative.
questions.explanation: X Theory presents the opposite assumptions. Independence and creativity under suitable conditions belong to Y Theory.

questions.question: Under Y Theory, most people can enjoy work when—
questions.explanation: The first stated assumption of Y Theory is that given the right conditions most people can enjoy work.

questions.question: Which pair belongs specifically to Y Theory?
options: Close supervision and lack of discretion
Inability to contribute and dislike of work
questions.explanation: Y Theory states that people can exercise self-control and be independent and creative under appropriate conditions.

questions.question: The seminar associate’s motivation under Y Theory with a group setting where people are—
questions.explanation: The material specifically states that motivation is necessary in a group setting where people are recognized and rewarded.

questions.question: A manager adopts a policy based on the belief that staff perform better when recognised and rewarded.
questions.explanation: Recognition and rewards are expressly associated with motivation under Y Theory.

questions.question: Which reform is most directly associated by its name with reducing the size of an organisation or sector to an appropriate level?
questions.explanation: Right-sizing is listed among the different types of public/civil service reforms. The seminar later states one of the reform goals as to right-size the sector and eliminate ghost workers.

questions.question: Which reform objective is directly associated with the problem of ghost workers?
questions.explanation: One of the stated goals of public-sector reforms is to right-size the sector and eliminate ghost workers.

questions.question: A reform programme seeks to improve the professional standards of civil servants.
options: Restore the professionalism of the Civil Service
Reduce the price of imported items
questions.explanation: Restoring the professionalism of the Civil Service is expressly identified as a public-sector reform goal.

questions.question: Which combination consists entirely of stated goals of the Public Sector Reforms?
options: Right-size the sector, restore professionalism, rationalize/restructure institutions
Increase bureaucracy, reduce accountability, expand ghost workers
Abolish institutions, increase waste, reduce transparency
Eliminate training, privatize every government function, suspend oversight
questions.explanation: The seminar lists right-sizing/eliminating ghost workers, restoring professionalism, and rationalizing/restructuring/strengthening institutions among the reform goals.

questions.question: Which reform goal deals most directly with reducing unnecessary government spending?
options: Reduce waste and improve efficiency of government expenditures
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly identifies reducing waste and improving efficiency of government expenditures as a reform goal.

questions.question: A reform programme seeks to improve transparency in public accounts while tackling corruption.
options: Tackle corruption and improve transparency in public accounts
Reduce the number of government policies
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically states the goal of tackling corruption and improving transparency in public accounts of government agencies and venture oil companies.

questions.question: A reform package simultaneously seeks to reduce government waste, strengthen institutions, tackle corruption and improve the responsiveness of the public sector.
options: The reforms are primarily designed to increase bureaucracy and managerial restrictions.
The reforms seek to address shortcomings in the public sector by making it more efficient and responsive while improving accountability and tackling corruption.
The reforms are concerned exclusively with pension administration.
The reforms are designed mainly to increase political control over the Civil Service.
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the reforms aim to address shortcomings in the public sector by creating a more efficient and responsive public sector, improving security and administration of justice, tackling corruption, and promoting transparency and accountability.

questions.question: Which of the following is the odd one out in the seminar's list of different types of reforms and effects in the Public/Civil Service?
questions.explanation: The seminar lists Rebranding, Right-sizing and Needs, Seeds, Leeds among the different reforms/effects. Annual Appropriation Law is not included in that particular list.

questions.question: Which combination contains only items explicitly listed under “Different Types of Reforms and Effects”?
options: Financial Instructions, Scheme of Service, Purge
questions.explanation: Purge, Re-organization and Right-sizing all appear in the seminar's reform list. The other options mix reform items with management tools or other concepts.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the reform list in the seminar?
questions.explanation: Whistle Blowing appears explicitly in the list of different reforms and effects. IPSAS, Financial Instructions and Schemes of Service also appear elsewhere in the broader list of management tools/concepts, but not as the specific item identified in this pairing.

questions.question: A candidate is asked to identify an item from the seminar's reform list that begins with the concept of making government institutions appropriately sized.
questions.explanation: Right-sizing is expressly listed among the reform types/effects.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed in the seminar after “Due Process” and before “Bureaucracy”?
questions.explanation: The sequence given is Due Process → Whistle Blowing → Bureaucracy.

questions.question: Which sequence reproduces the seminar's ordering of these listed reform/effect concepts?
options: Purge → Re-organization → Needs, Seeds, Leeds → Right-sizing
Purge → Right-sizing → Re-organization → Needs, Seeds, Leeds
Needs, Seeds, Leeds → Purge → Rebranding → Right-sizing
questions.explanation: The seminar presents the sequence Purge, Re-organization, Needs, Seeds, Leeds, Right-sizing.

questions.question: Which pair appears in the seminar's list of reform/effect concepts but is not a pair of personnel-management records?
options: Pro-rata leave and Leave of absence
questions.explanation: Servicom and IPSAS are both explicitly listed among the different reform/effect concepts.

questions.question: The seminar lists “Termination, Dismissal, retirement, withdrawal and resignation of Appointment” together. Which conclusion is safest?
options: The seminar presents all five as forms of reform.
The seminar identifies all five within its broader list of concepts/effects to be noted.
Only termination and dismissal are listed.
Only retirement and resignation are listed.
questions.explanation: The seminar includes termination, dismissal, retirement, withdrawal and resignation of appointment as one of the listed areas to note.

questions.question: Which of the following is explicitly associated with Establishment Circulars 3/1988 and 2/2009 in the seminar?
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly gives Pooling system (Est. Cir. 3/1988, Est. CIR. 2/2009).

questions.question: Which item is correctly paired with CSC Circular 1/2000?
options: Guidelines for Appointment, Promotions and Discipline
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies CSC Circular 1/2000 as providing guidelines for Appointment, Promotions and Discipline.

questions.question: The Ayida's Report of 1996 is identified in the seminar as—
options: a major reform in the Civil Service
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly describes Ayida's Report on Civil Service Reforms (1996) as a major reform in the Civil Service.

questions.question: Which combination correctly matches the 1999 Constitution (as amended) with the subject identified in the seminar?
options: Sections 206 and 210 — establishment of State Service and protection of pension rights
Sections 010101 and 010107 — establishment of State Service
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically associates Sections 206 and 210 with the establishment of State Service and protection of pension rights.

questions.question: Which statement about the 2022 Public Service Rules is directly supported by the seminar?
options: They are concerned only with financial administration.
They embody rules and regulations guiding the operation or changes in the Service.
They apply only to senior officers.
They can be amended informally by any manager.
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the 2022 Edition of the PSR embodies rules and regulations that guide the operation or changes in the Service.

questions.question: According to the seminar, Section 010101 of the Public Service Rules is particularly important because it requires—
options: all Public/Civil Servants to be acquainted with the provisions of the Rules
all officers to retire after ten years
all circulars to be cancelled annually
all promotion examinations to be computer-based
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically directs attention to Section 010101, which contains the mandatory order for Public/Civil Servants to be acquainted with the provisions of the Rules.

questions.question: Which statement correctly reflects the seminar's treatment of Section 010107?
options: It provides for amendments to the Public Service Rules only through circular.
It establishes the Pension Reform system.
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically identifies Section 010107 as dealing with amendments to the Rules only through circular.

questions.question: A manager claims that because a Public Service Rule is inconvenient, he can simply alter the wording in an internal memorandum.
options: Correct, because every manager can amend PSRs.
Incorrect; the seminar specifically identifies Section 010107 as requiring amendments to the Rules through circular.
Correct, provided the officer is a Director.
Incorrect only if the rule concerns finance.
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly identifies Section 010107 as providing for amendments to the Rules only through circular.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed immediately among the management/reform concepts surrounding the PSRs in the seminar?
questions.explanation: The seminar lists Financial Regulations, the legislative oversight function, the constitutional provisions and PSRs among the relevant concepts. Electoral ward delimitation is not listed.

questions.question: The seminar's discussion of public-sector reforms states that they arose against a background that included—
options: persistent low performance of the Nigerian economy and widespread poverty
excessive economic growth and low unemployment
questions.explanation: The seminar explicitly states that the reforms were developed against the background of persistent low performance of the Nigerian economy and widespread poverty.

questions.question: The wide-ranging public-sector reforms identified in the seminar were part of the overall development framework encapsulated by—
options: the National Economic Empowerment and Development Strategy (NEEDS)
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically identifies NEEDS — National Economic Empowerment and Development Strategy as the framework within which the reforms were encapsulated.

questions.question: Which statement BEST describes the broad purpose of the public-sector reforms?
options: To preserve existing shortcomings in government operations
To change how government works by creating a more efficient and responsive public sector
To concentrate government activity exclusively on taxation
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the reforms seek to change the way government does its work by creating a more efficient and responsive public sector.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT expressly identified as a broad area the reforms seek to address?
options: Improving security and administration of justice
Expanding political-party membership in the Civil Service
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies security, administration of justice, corruption, transparency and accountability. Political-party membership is not identified as a reform objective.

questions.question: Which reform objective specifically combines an institutional objective with a personnel problem?
options: Right-size the sector and eliminate ghost workers
questions.explanation: Right-sizing the sector and eliminating ghost workers is expressly stated as one combined reform goal.

questions.question: A reform programme seeks to reorganize institutions so that they become stronger and more appropriately structured.
questions.explanation: The exact reform goal given is to rationalize, restructure and strengthen institutions.

questions.question: Which reform goal would most directly involve opening the public sector to private participation and reducing restrictions?
questions.explanation: The seminar explicitly identifies privatizing and liberalizing the sector as a public-sector reform goal.

questions.question: Which objective is most directly concerned with the quality and ethical standing of civil servants?
options: Restore the professionalism of the Civil Service
questions.explanation: Restoring the professionalism of the Civil Service is one of the seminar's stated reform goals.

questions.question: A reform initiative seeks to reduce unnecessary government spending while obtaining greater value from expenditure.
options: Reduce waste and improve efficiency of government expenditures
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly identifies reducing waste and improving efficiency of government expenditures as a reform goal.

questions.question: Which reform objective is the most directly macroeconomic/coordinating in wording?
questions.explanation: Among the listed objectives, enhance economic coordination is the one explicitly framed around economic coordination.

questions.question: Which pair of reform objectives deals respectively with institutional restructuring and economic management?
options: Rationalize, restructure and strengthen institutions / Enhance economic coordination
questions.explanation: The first objective is explicitly institutional, while enhancing economic coordination is separately identified as an economic reform objective.

questions.question: Which of the following combinations contains only stated public-sector reform goals?
options: MBWA, Scheme of Service, written promotion examination
X Theory, Y Theory, democratic leadership
questions.explanation: All three—right-sizing, restoration of professionalism, and privatization/liberalization—are expressly listed as public-sector reform goals.

questions.question: A candidate claims that “right-sizing” and “restoring professionalism” are essentially the same reform objective because both improve the Civil Service.
options: Correct; the seminar treats them as synonyms.
Incorrect; the seminar lists them as separate goals—one concerns the size of the sector and ghost workers, while the other concerns professionalism.
Incorrect because neither is a reform objective.
questions.explanation: The seminar separately lists right-sizing/eliminating ghost workers and restoring professionalism as distinct reform goals.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best-supported distinction between “rationalize, restructure and strengthen institutions” and “reduce waste and improve efficiency of government expenditures”?
options: The first concerns institutions; the second concerns government expenditure.
Both refer exclusively to personnel recruitment.
The first concerns pensions; the second concerns political appointments.
They are two names for the same objective.
questions.explanation: The seminar lists the two separately: one focuses on institutions, while the other specifically concerns waste and efficiency of government expenditures.

questions.question: Which combination contains a reform goal relating to accountability/transparency in public accounts?
options: Tackle corruption and improve transparency in public accounts
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly identifies tackling corruption and improving transparency in public accounts of government agencies and venture oil companies as a reform goal.

questions.question: A reform proposal contains four objectives:
options: Only 1 and 2 are supported by the seminar.
All four are expressly stated reform goals.
None is stated as a reform goal.
questions.explanation: All four appear in the seminar's stated Goals of the Public Sector Reforms.

questions.question: Which of the following would be the least directly connected to the reform objectives listed in the seminar?
options: Increasing the number of ghost workers
questions.explanation: The reform goal is to eliminate ghost workers, not increase them. The other three are explicitly stated objectives.

questions.question: The seminar's conclusion says managers of the Public/Civil Service have used various management techniques through—
options: various reforms from the pre-colonial era till date
questions.explanation: The conclusion states that managers have used various management techniques through various reforms during the pre-colonial era till date.

questions.question: Which statement is most consistent with the seminar's conclusion regarding management techniques?
options: Management techniques in government have remained unchanged.
Various reforms have been used as management techniques over time.
Reforms have no relationship with management.
Only private organisations use management techniques.
questions.explanation: The conclusion explicitly links various reforms with the management techniques used by Public/Civil Service managers over time.

questions.question: The conclusion specifically tells candidates to pay attention to the issue of—
options: replacement of APOCE with interviews only
questions.explanation: The seminar conclusion specifically mentions the issue of Computer Based Test in recruitment exercise among recent management actions.

questions.question: Which of the following is mentioned in the conclusion as a feature of APOCE?
questions.explanation: The conclusion explicitly mentions the issue of multiple-choice questions in APOCE and the application of computer-based APOCE.

questions.question: The conclusion refers to CSC Circular 2017 specifically in connection with—
options: passing an examination before promotion to Grade Level 14
questions.explanation: The seminar conclusion refers to CSC Circular 2017 on passing this examination before promotion to Grade Level 14.

questions.question: Which statement correctly combines two examination-related developments mentioned in the conclusion?
options: Written examination before promotion and computer-based APOCE
Abolition of promotion examinations and oral APOCE
Written recruitment only and abolition of CBT
questions.explanation: The conclusion identifies the issue of written examination before promotion and the application of computer-based APOCE among the management actions discussed.

questions.question: A candidate says the seminar treats examination changes merely as academic matters unrelated to management.
options: Incorrect; the conclusion presents written promotion examinations, CBT recruitment and computer-based APOCE as examples of management actions/techniques.
Correct; only reforms before independence count as management techniques.
Incorrect because examinations are exclusively financial controls.
questions.explanation: The conclusion explicitly places written promotion examinations, CBT recruitment, multiple-choice APOCE and computer-based APOCE among the management actions discussed.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT among the specific examination/recruitment developments mentioned in the seminar's conclusion?
options: Replacement of CBT with handwritten examination in APOCE
questions.explanation: The seminar mentions the opposite: the application of computer-based APOCE, alongside CBT recruitment and multiple-choice questions.

questions.question: The seminar's treatment of the internal and external environment ultimately requires managers to—
options: overcome or manage the challenges posed by both environments
questions.explanation: In its conclusion, the seminar specifically refers to the internal/external environment, noting that managers will have to overcome the two environments.

questions.question: Which scenario BEST demonstrates why the distinction between internal and external environment matters?
options: A manager considers both staff capabilities inside the organisation and government policies affecting its operations.
A manager considers only the office furniture.
A manager ignores clients and suppliers.
A manager considers only the organisation's name.
questions.explanation: The seminar distinguishes internal factors such as personnel, objectives and technology from external factors such as clients, suppliers, economic variables and government policies.

questions.question: A manager wants to select a management technique for a particular operational problem. According to the seminar, the selection should primarily consider—
options: what best contributes to organisational or societal goals in that particular situation and time
what another organisation used regardless of circumstances
only the cost of the technique
questions.explanation: The seminar says managers should identify methods or techniques that best contribute to organisational or societal goals in a particular situation and time.

questions.question: Which statement is most faithful to the seminar's treatment of management resources?
options: Managers should focus only on current resource availability.
Managers face the task of harnessing resources while considering continued availability, goals and differences in environment.
Resources are irrelevant if organisational goals are clear.
Only human resources matter in management.
questions.explanation: The seminar explicitly identifies harnessing resources, continued availability of resources, goals and environmental differences as concerns facing managers.

questions.question: A manager copies a technique from another organisation without considering the difference in circumstances, time or goals.
options: Management techniques should be appropriate to the particular situation and time.
Management is exclusively about financial control.
Techniques are identical in every organisation.
questions.explanation: The seminar emphasizes identifying management methods that contribute to goals in a particular situation and time, rather than treating techniques as universally interchangeable.

questions.question: Which combination contains only external management-environment factors expressly identified in the seminar?
questions.explanation: The external environment includes end users/beneficiaries, suppliers/providers and economic variables, as well as political atmosphere, insecurity and government policies.

questions.question: A government policy on taxation changes the attractiveness of investment in a sector.
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically states that fiscal or tax policies can affect investment or business positively or negatively and places such matters within the external environment.

questions.question: A manager is confronted simultaneously with:
options: Apply one fixed technique regardless of circumstances.
Abandon organisational goals until the environment becomes stable.
Harness available resources and select management methods appropriate to the particular situation and time.
Focus exclusively on the internal environment and ignore external factors.
questions.explanation: This combines the seminar's central management ideas: managers must harness resources, consider their continued availability, goals and environmental differences, and identify techniques that best contribute to organisational or societal goals in a particular situation and time.

questions.question: Which statement BEST captures the seminar's conception of management?
options: The process of maximizing financial profit regardless of resources
The continuous search for optimum use of resources in pursuit of desired goals
The process of controlling employees through punishment
The process of enforcing government regulations only
questions.explanation: The seminar defines management as the process of continuous search for the optimum use of resources in pursuit of desired goals.

questions.question: An officer says, “A management technique is simply a rule governing conduct.”
options: A principle is a way of achieving one's purpose skillfully, while technique is a rule.
A principle is a set of rules guiding conduct, while a technique is a way of achieving one's purpose skillfully.
Principles and techniques mean exactly the same thing.
Technique refers exclusively to financial procedures.
questions.explanation: The seminar defines principles as rules guiding conduct/norms/procedures, while a technique is a way of achieving one's purpose skillfully.

questions.question: Which combination is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: All three definitions appear in the seminar.

questions.question: A manager has abundant resources but uses them wastefully and fails to achieve organisational goals.
options: Optimum use of resources in pursuit of desired goals
questions.explanation: The seminar places optimum use of resources and desired goals at the heart of management.

questions.question: Two organisations face different operating environments. The seminar suggests that their managers should—
options: identify techniques best suited to their particular situations and times
questions.explanation: Managers are expected to identify methods/techniques that best contribute to organisational or societal goals in a particular situation and time.

questions.question: Which of the following belongs to the internal management environment?
questions.explanation: The internal environment includes the organisation's type, size and location; objectives; managers/personnel; and technology, facilities and equipment.

questions.question: Which combination contains only internal environmental factors?
questions.explanation: Those three are explicitly listed under the internal environment.

questions.question: Which factor is classified as an external management environment even though it can directly affect the organisation's operations?
questions.explanation: Fiscal or tax policies are expressly listed under the external environment.

questions.question: An MDA's computers, office equipment and technological systems are being assessed.
questions.explanation: Technology, facilities, equipment and tools are identified as components of the internal management environment.

questions.question: A ministry experiences difficulty because the price of imported equipment suddenly rises.
options: an economic variable within the external environment
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically gives an increase in the price of imported items as an example of an economic variable in the external environment.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified as an external environmental factor?
questions.explanation: Managers and other personnel, including their background and attitude, are part of the internal environment.

questions.question: A government agency's beneficiaries suddenly change their expectations of service.
questions.explanation: End users or beneficiaries—including clients, customers and members of the public—are identified as external environmental constituents.

questions.question: Statutory allocation received by a government organisation is used in the seminar as an example associated with—
questions.explanation: The seminar lists suppliers/providers of funds, labour, technology or infrastructure, giving statutory allocation as an example.

questions.question: Which scenario contains one internal and one external environmental factor, in that order?
questions.explanation: Managers/personnel and their attitudes are internal; fiscal/tax policy is external.

questions.question: The seminar's historical discussion says the restructuring of the Civil Service was driven by the need for Nigeria's Civil Service to—
options: meet global, technical and transformational demands
questions.explanation: The seminar says Nigeria needed its Civil Service to be radically changed to meet globally, technically and transformation demands.

questions.question: Which historical figure is associated in the seminar with the Great Purge?
questions.explanation: The seminar states that Murtala Mohammed applied a restructuring measure referred to as the Great Purge.

questions.question: Which statement is most consistent with the seminar's treatment of the Great Purge?
options: It was presented as a Civil Service restructuring measure.
It was a personnel motivation scheme.
It was a form of APER.
questions.explanation: The Great Purge is introduced in the seminar specifically within the discussion of the restructuring of the Civil Service.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four listed components of the internal management environment?
options: Type, size and location of organisation
questions.explanation: Political atmosphere is listed under the external environment.

questions.question: Which combination correctly classifies the following?
questions.explanation: Objectives and technology are internal; economic variables and suppliers/providers are external.

questions.question: A manager argues: “Since government policy is outside my organisation, it has nothing to do with management.”
options: Incorrect; government policies form part of the external environment and may affect investment or business positively or negatively.
Correct, unless the policy concerns taxation.
Incorrect only because government policy is an internal factor.
questions.explanation: The seminar explicitly places government policies in the external environment and notes that fiscal/tax policies can affect investment or business positively or negatively.

questions.question: Which statement about the Civil/Public Service is supported by the seminar?
options: It exists only for the duration of a political administration.
It enjoys continuity of existence and serves as an instrument of the government of the day.
It is independent of government policy.
questions.explanation: The seminar describes Civil/Public Service as a body that enjoys continuity of existence and as an instrument of the Government of the day.

questions.question: The seminar describes the Civil Service as being composed of persons employed in a—
options: civil capacity and on a non-political career basis
questions.explanation: It describes civil servants as servants of the state employed in a civil capacity and non-political career basis.

questions.question: Which of the following best captures the seminar's description of the Civil Service as a “prepared place for prepared people”?
options: Officers are expected to operate without rules.
Officers are prepared through ethics, rules, dress code and related expectations.
Officers are selected only through political appointments.
Officers are not required to follow established procedures.
questions.explanation: The seminar uses the phrase in connection with ethics, rules, dress code, creed, etc.

questions.question: Which constitutional provisions are listed as a management tool/concept concerning the establishment of State Service and protection of pension rights?
questions.explanation: The seminar explicitly identifies Sections 206 and 210 for this purpose.

questions.question: Which body is identified as implementing government policies?
questions.explanation: The seminar lists the National Council on Establishments as a body to implement government policies.

questions.question: Circulars/circular letters are described as instruments used to—
options: amend, cancel or institute new rules for implementation in the Service
questions.explanation: The seminar states that circulars/circular letters provide guidelines and are issued regularly to amend, cancel or institute new rules for implementation.

questions.question: Which statement about circulars is MOST accurate according to the seminar?
options: They are regularly issued guidelines affecting changes in rules and regulations and must be obeyed by all.
They apply only to political office holders.
They are inferior to personal instructions from any senior officer.
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly says circulars/circular letters are issued regularly for changes in rules and must be obeyed by all.

questions.question: Which circular is associated with re-alignment of nomenclature and functional titles of some cadres approved in the Scheme of Service?
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically identifies the SSG Circular of 14 July 1998 for this purpose.

questions.question: According to the seminar, Ministries generally have what kind of responsibility?
questions.explanation: The seminar says other Ministries' responsibilities are regarded as Mono-function (single), while the Governor's Office is heterogeneous/dual-functions.

questions.question: Which combination contains only functions listed under the heterogeneous/dual-functions of the Governor's Office?
options: Constitutional matters, prerogative of mercy, appointment of key public functionaries
Scheme of Service, Financial Instructions, APER
questions.explanation: The seminar lists constitutional matters, relations with the Presidency/Assemblies, prerogative of mercy, state security/public safety, appointment of key public functionaries, and relations with Armed Forces and Police, among others.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT expressly listed as a Governor's Office heterogeneous function?
options: State security matters and public safety
Relations with the Armed Forces and Police
questions.explanation: APER is listed elsewhere as a personnel-management tool; it is not listed among the Governor's Office heterogeneous functions.

questions.question: The Scheme of Service is described as showing—
options: different cadres, entry, progression and qualification
questions.explanation: Those four elements are explicitly listed in the seminar.

questions.question: Financial Instructions are identified as providing guidelines for—
options: receipts and expenditure of government funds
questions.explanation: The seminar directly states that Financial Instructions provide guidelines for receipts and expenditure of government funds.

questions.question: The Pension Reforms Act 2014 is presented in the seminar as marking a departure from—
questions.explanation: The seminar says the Act represented a clear departure from the former pay-as-you-go system to the contributory system of retirement-benefit payment.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Service Delivery Charter from the Scheme of Service?
options: The Charter concerns improved performance, accountability, transparency and service delivery; the Scheme of Service shows cadres, entry, progression and qualification.
The Charter governs pension contributions while the Scheme governs tax policy.
Both are names for the same document.
questions.explanation: The seminar gives these distinct functions for the two instruments.

questions.question: Which training institutions are specifically mentioned as examples of seminars/workshops and training opportunities?
questions.explanation: The seminar mentions the Centre for Management Development (CMD) and Administrative Staff College of Nigeria (ASCON).

questions.question: Which statement about leadership is directly supported by the seminar?
options: All managers are leaders, but not all leaders are managers.
Leadership has no relationship with communication.
questions.explanation: The seminar explicitly makes this distinction.

questions.question: According to the seminar, leadership is highly behavioural and calls for all of the following EXCEPT—
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically mentions intelligence, communication, moral building, motivation, human relationships, charisma and maturity.

questions.question: A leader who possesses intelligence but cannot communicate effectively is lacking one of the qualities the seminar associates with—
questions.explanation: Good communication is expressly identified as part of effective leadership.

questions.question: Which pair represents two qualities of good leadership specifically listed in the seminar?
options: Fairness and ability to handle emergencies without panicking
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies a good leader as fair, approachable but firm, and able to handle emergencies without panicking.

questions.question: Which leadership quality most directly concerns the ability to anticipate beyond the immediate capabilities of subordinates?
questions.explanation: The seminar defines vision as the ability to see or think beyond the limits of followers or subordinates.

questions.question: According to the seminar, a good leader should—
options: accept change but avoid influencing it
not only accept change but act as a change agent
questions.explanation: The seminar explicitly says a leader should not only be willing to accept change but should be a change agent.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the seminar's recommended leadership style?
questions.explanation: “Fair, approachable but firm” is directly stated among the qualities of good leadership.

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a problem of leadership in an organisation?
options: Multiplicity of interest groups and ethnic nationalities
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies the multiplicity of interest groups and ethnic nationalities as a leadership problem.

questions.question: Which combination contains only problems of leadership identified in the seminar?
options: Poverty/patriotic mentality problem, multiplicity of interest groups, rapid turnover in political leadership
questions.explanation: These are explicitly identified under Problems of Leadership in Organisation.

questions.question: Why does the seminar identify rapid turnover in political leadership as a leadership problem?
options: Because it contributes to a short span of continuity in government policy and thinking.
Because it eliminates all government employees.
Because it prevents every form of delegation.
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically identifies short span of continuity in government policy and rapid turnover in political leadership and thinking as a problem.

questions.question: Which management technique is explicitly expanded in the seminar as Management by Walking Around?
questions.explanation: The seminar explicitly gives MBWA = Management by Walking Around.

questions.question: Which statement about the X and Y theories is supported by the seminar?
options: X Theory assumes people can enjoy work under right conditions.
Y Theory assumes people can exercise self-control and can be independent and creative under suitable conditions.
Y Theory is based exclusively on punishment.
X Theory emphasizes recognition and reward.
questions.explanation: The seminar's Y Theory principles include that, under the right conditions, people can enjoy work, exercise self-control, and be independent and creative; motivation also matters where people are recognized and rewarded.

questions.question: A supervisor believes employees generally dislike work, cannot be trusted to work independently, and respond mainly when threatened or punished.
questions.explanation: The seminar's X Theory principles include assumptions that people do not like to work, require close supervision, cannot contribute creatively and may work only when threatened or punished.

questions.question: A Director says:
options: Correct; delegation transfers the manager's job permanently to subordinates.
Incorrect; delegation transfers accountability for results down the line, creates trust, trains staff indirectly, and allows the manager to concentrate on the real job.
Correct; delegation is appropriate only for junior officers.
Incorrect only because delegation removes accountability from the manager.
questions.explanation: The seminar describes delegation as a process through which accountability for results is transferred down the line. It says delegation creates trust, serves as an indirect means of training staff, speeds achievement of results, and is not giving away your job but getting people to do their jobs so you can focus on your real job.
